title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §3 of a manuscript on moduli of elliptic curves when the residue characteristics are ≠2. It is titled roughly 'Relations avec courbes elliptiques; le morphisme f_2^ε : Σ_J → Σ_J'' (reading uncertain). The preceding pages build objects Σ_J, which appear to be relative P^1's (or forms of them) with a 4-element set J of marked points. They also introduce a Klein-four-group scheme V and V-torsors I. This section links those genus-0 objects to genus-1 curves.

Setup: S is a base scheme on which 2 is invertible. E_0/S is an elliptic curve and E is an E_0-torsor, i.e. a smooth proper genus-1 curve with Pic^0_{E/S} ≅ E_0. One is given an S-automorphism σ of E whose induced action on E_0 = Pic^0 is −id.

Step 1. Étale-locally choose an origin, which identifies E with E_0. Then σ(x) = a − x for a suitable section a. Intrinsically, a = x + σ(x) is a section of E ∧^{E_0} E ≅ Pic^1 ∧ Pic^1 ≅ Pic^2_{E/S}. Hence σ² = id, so σ is an involution.

Step 2. The fixed-point subscheme I = E^σ = {x ∈ E | 2x = a} is the fibre over a of the doubling map E → Pic^2_{E/S}. That map is an étale torsor under V = E_0[2] = Ker(2: E_0 → E_0), since 2 is invertible. So I is a V-torsor, where V is étale-locally isomorphic to the constant Klein group (Z/2)^2.

Step 3 (begun here, finished on the next page). The data (E, σ) are equivalent to the data (E_0, I) with I a V-torsor, via:
- E = I ∧^V E_0, i.e. the E_0-torsor obtained by pushing I along V ⊂ E_0;
- σ induced from x ↦ −x.

On the next page Grothendieck takes quotients X = E/⟨σ⟩ and Σ = E_0/⟨−1⟩, which are P^1-bundles. Then V acts on X with X/V ≅ Σ, and the branch loci are respectively the V-torsor I and the 2-torsion. This is the torsor-theoretic, base-free version of the classical correspondence (Legendre / level-2 structure): a genus-1 double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points, and λ-line / M_{0,4} ↔ M(2). It is presumably used to define the morphism f_2^ε between the Σ_J's.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The claim that I is a V-torsor tacitly uses that doubling E → Pic^2 is finite étale of degree 4, which holds because 2 is invertible on S (assumed). The phrase 'cela veut dire que E_0 ≃ Pic^0_{E/S}' is a slight abuse: being an E_0-torsor identifies E_0 with Pic^0 canonically up to sign convention. It is correct.

ideas.what: A genus-1 curve E (torsor under E_0) with an involution acting as −1 on Pic^0 has σ(x) = a − x, with a an intrinsic section of E∧E ≅ Pic^2_{E/S}
ideas.modern_name: hyperelliptic-type involution of a genus one curve; degree-2 divisor class determined by x + σ(x)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (folklore in descent theory of genus one curves)

ideas.what: Fixed-point scheme of σ is a torsor under E_0[2], and (E,σ) ↔ (E_0, E_0[2]-torsor I) with E = I ∧^{E_0[2]} E_0
ideas.modern_name: 2-coverings / image of H^1(S,E[2]) → H^1(S,E); Weierstrass points as an E[2]-torsor

ideas.what: Quotients E/σ and E_0/±1 are P^1-bundles with X/V ≅ Σ, relating elliptic curves to P^1 with 4 marked points (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family; isomorphism of level-2 modular curve with M_{0,4}; Kummer line
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi); modern relative treatments e.g. Katz–Mazur

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, base-free torsor formulation of the classical correspondence between genus-1 curves with involution, E_0[2]-torsors, and P^1 with 4 branch points. It is standard material, carefully organized, and contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ce qui est d'ailleurs intrinsèque ni [?] — indépendant [?] — E∧_{E_0}E ≃ Pic^2_{E/S}. a comme une section de' should read: 'ce qui est d'ailleurs intrinsèque si on interprète a comme une section de E∧_{E_0}E ≃ Pic^2_{E/S}'.
(18) reads σ^~_{E_0} = −id_{E_0}: the induced action of σ on E_0. The superscript is a tilde-like mark, not ε.
'loc. isom. à 𝔻_S' is probably 'loc. isom. à V_S' (constant Klein four-group), consistent with the notation V_S on the previous page; the curly addition is 'sur S'.
'On suppose donné dans E un S-automorphisme' — the 'S-' is written above the word.
'On suppose toujours les car. rés. de S ≠ 2' is correct.
